related_questions.question: What is the contagious period of COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: A person with COVID-19 is generally considered infectious starting up to 48 hours before symptoms appear. The infectious period typically lasts until at least 24 hours after symptoms are improving overall and the individual has been fever-free without medication. The risk of transmission is highest during close, face-to-face contact, but can occur over larger distances, especially indoors.

text_blocks.snippet: You can start being contagious with COVID-19 on the same day you are exposed to the virus. Viral shedding, which is how viruses spread, can occur as soon as you pick up the virus. Some individuals may begin shedding the virus 2-3 days before symptoms appear. According to GoodRx, people are generally most contagious when their viral load is highest, which is typically 3 to 5 days after symptoms start.
